question: Should byte-triggered preflight compaction persist per-session retry state and wait for max(1 MiB, 10%) growth before retrying the same active transcript?
rationale: The code is correct and proven, but the growth window deliberately trades fewer compaction loops for delayed byte-triggered retries and establishes new persisted session-state semantics.

options.title: Accept the hysteresis policy
options.body: Land the additive SessionEntry metadata and current growth threshold as the supported retry behavior.

options.title: Tune the retry window
options.body: Choose different absolute or relative growth criteria and update the focused regressions before merge.

options.title: Pause for broader compaction policy
options.body: Hold this PR if byte-triggered retry behavior should be resolved together with the opposite trigger semantics tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/88188.

recommendation.title: Accept the hysteresis policy
recommendation.body: Land the additive SessionEntry metadata and current growth threshold as the supported retry behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is recent work on the same preflight compaction decision surface.
